classification.difficultyReason: Reflect each supplied branch in the y-axis, preserving heights, intercepts, endpoints and asymptotic behaviour; part (d) also maps the minimum from (-1,1) to (1,1).

content.prompt: Complete the following diagrams to make the graphs represent even functions.

spec.description: Unnumbered coordinate axes with the supplied first-quadrant rising curve and its continuation arrow. The left half-plane remains available for drawing.
spec.mathematics: Schematic curve through the origin. No equation or numerical scale is supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: The reflected branch is hidden in the question edition.

answer.short: Add the mirror image of the supplied curve in the $y$-axis.
answer.worked: For an even function, $f(-x)=f(x)$. Reflect each point $(x,y)$ to $(-x,y)$. The added branch rises into the second quadrant and meets the supplied branch at the origin.

spec.description: Missing branch reflected exactly in the y-axis, using the base coordinate frame and bounding box.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only, superimposed on the supplied graph.

spec.description: Positive reciprocal-like branch approaching both positive coordinate axes, with arrows at both ends and no ticks or grid.
spec.mathematics: Unscaled schematic branch in the first quadrant. Its equation is unspecified.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the source branch is visible.

answer.short: Add a matching positive branch in the second quadrant, reflected in the $y$-axis.
answer.worked: For an even function, $f(-x)=f(x)$. Reflect the supplied branch in the $y$-axis. The new branch approaches the negative $x$-axis and the positive $y$-axis.

spec.description: Second-quadrant reflection with continuation arrows, using the exact base frame.
spec.mathematics: Equal positive heights at opposite x-values.

spec.description: Supplied positive left-hand curve rising to the marked y-intercept 2, with an arrow toward the negative x-axis.
spec.mathematics: The only numerical given is the y-intercept 2. The curve's equation is unspecified.

answer.short: Reflect the curve in the $y$-axis. The completed graph passes through $(0,2)$.
answer.worked: Apply $(x,y)\mapsto(-x,y)$. Draw the reflected curve to the right of the $y$-axis, keeping the point $(0,2)$ fixed and approaching the positive $x$-axis.

spec.description: Exact y-axis reflection of the supplied curve in the base frame.
Left-hand trough with minimum (-1,1), dashed guides and a filled positive y-axis endpoint whose height is unlabelled.
spec.mathematics: Only the minimum coordinates are numerical givens. The drawing coordinate used for the unlabelled endpoint conveys schematic placement.

answer.short: Reflect in the $y$-axis, adding a trough with minimum $(1,1)$.
answer.worked: Reflect each point using $(x,y)\mapsto(-x,y)$. The minimum $(-1,1)$ maps to $(1,1)$. The filled point on the $y$-axis stays fixed, and the outer branches rise on both sides.

spec.description: Mirrored trough meeting the existing filled endpoint. Original numerical guides remain visible in the base.
